items.title: Lionel Ferbos Interview, 1964-08-03
items.q: The interviewee does not mention the King Brothers; the interviewer mentions them in relation to Nat Story, and the interviewee does not confirm or deny any personal connection to the King Brothers themselves.

ctx.x: That's right, ages 4. And did the father play with Pichon? No, a father from out of, I don't know if he was from out of Alabama or someplace, I can't think of his name, he was a tall slender boy who was playing trombone and in the sax station he had Theodore Poinnell, Joyce Clark and I think Bodley. Yeah, Bodley was playing I think for a while. And then he had Judge Riley playing drum. Who Sam was with then? Sam who? Sam who? Oh no, he wasn't with them. Judge Riley playing drum. And Walter on piano. And then he…

He and the King Brothers I think, I met him at the same time. They had two brothers, King Brothers, both of them played trumpet and I think Nat was playing trombone with him, playing with Faith's all the time.

And then he was playing trombone with him. And then he was playing with Faith's all the time. And then I even took a license with Albert Snyder. He used to work on the Capitol with Faith too for a long time. And the band with Robichaud, you remember?
